claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90 + distance $23.84 for 16.9 km + time $8.45 for 32.5 min, no waiting fee, no surge), so detour kilometres flow straight into the fare the rider paid.

There is one off-route segment (18:26–18:38) that drove 10.27 km where the optimal route covers 9.43 km, adding 0.84 km, and the track sits up to 2831 m off the optimal route — a genuine deviation, not map-matching noise.

The driver's reroute is not justified by road conditions: the only incident (F13) is an accident on KPE at the MCE tunnel entrance at 18:02 with all lanes closed, but the off-route segment did not begin until 18:26 and the optimal route the rider complains about runs via the KPE corridor; the driver's own chat says he switched to ECP, whose speed band was 7 (60–69 km/h) — free-flowing, not a blocked route.

The KPE congestion band 1 (0–9 km/h) recorded 18:00–18:45 (F10) only corroborates the incident evidence and cannot by itself exempt the segment, and it says nothing about whether the 0.84 km extra on the ECP detour was necessary.

Even if the driver was entitled to avoid KPE, his own stated route was the ECP (F7/F11), which is a different corridor from the 0.84 km of extra distance recorded 18:26–18:38, so that excess was not shown to be justified.

The rider's agreement message (18:10) came before the segment start (18:26), so on its face it is timely; but the rider only assented to 'go by ECP', which does not cover extra distance off the agreed corridor, so no more than the ECP corridor itself can be treated as consented.

On these facts the metered overcharge recoverable under the policy is the unexempted segment's extra distance valued at the trip's own per-km rate: 0.84 km × $1.41/km = $1.18, which is consistent with the $1.85 total excess-distance billed for the whole 1.3 km of extra driving (the residual 0.46 km being residual matching difference, not refundable).

No fares beyond the meter plus published additions were added (waiting fee $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge), so the disputed $2 the rider noticed is the mileage/time effect of the extra 1.3 km and 11.2 minutes, not an unpublished charge.

The driver has 910 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes, and the rider has 1 upheld route dispute in 90 days; the profile record therefore does not show the driver as a repeat offender and is offered only as background, not as the basis for the finding.

weaknesses: The driver's reroute has real support: F13 shows a genuine accident on the KPE at the MCE tunnel entrance at 18:02 with all lanes closed, and F10 shows KPE at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) throughout 18:00–18:45 — the other side will argue under RD-4 that the alternative corridor was a reasonable cause, which could exempt the segment entirely.

The rider consented in chat to the ECP route (F7, F8) at 18:10, before the detour began at 18:26; the driver will argue under RD-5 that this is an agreed route change, and my attempt to limit consent to the 'ECP corridor' relies on reading F3's 0.84 km as outside that corridor rather than on an explicit limit in the messages.

The refund I request is small ($1.18) and I do not dispute the other $0.67 of the $1.85 excess-distance charge, so the driver can fairly say F4's billed excess is largely consistent with the driving actually done and the outcome should not be refund_full.

The rider's own profile (F15) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld — including a route dispute — which the driver may use to argue the rider habitually disputes metered fares, though RD-6 lets profiles never decide a case.

Traffic facts only show conditions on KPE/ECP/MCE corridors; there is no record of whether the specific extra 0.84 km stretch on the ECP was itself congested, so a strict RD-4 reading could leave that stretch exempt too.

claims.assertion: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (base $3.90 + distance $23.84 for 16.9 km + time $8.45 for 32.5 min, no waiting fee, no surge), so detour kilometres flow straight into the fare the rider paid.

There is one off-route segment (18:26–18:38) that drove 10.27 km where the optimal route covers 9.43 km, adding 0.84 km, and the track sits up to 2831 m off the optimal route — a genuine deviation, not map-matching noise.

The driver's reroute is not justified by road conditions: the only incident (F13) is an accident on KPE at the MCE tunnel entrance at 18:02 with all lanes closed, but the off-route segment did not begin until 18:26 and the optimal route the rider complains about runs via the KPE corridor; the driver's own chat says he switched to ECP, whose speed band was 7 (60–69 km/h) — free-flowing, not a blocked route.

The KPE congestion band 1 (0–9 km/h) recorded 18:00–18:45 (F10) only corroborates the incident evidence and cannot by itself exempt the segment, and it says nothing about whether the 0.84 km extra on the ECP detour was necessary.

Even if the driver was entitled to avoid KPE, his own stated route was the ECP (F7/F11), which is a different corridor from the 0.84 km of extra distance recorded 18:26–18:38, so that excess was not shown to be justified.

The rider's agreement message (18:10) came before the segment start (18:26), so on its face it is timely; but the rider only assented to 'go by ECP', which does not cover extra distance off the agreed corridor, so no more than the ECP corridor itself can be treated as consented.

On these facts the metered overcharge recoverable under the policy is the unexempted segment's extra distance valued at the trip's own per-km rate: 0.84 km × $1.41/km = $1.18, which is consistent with the $1.85 total excess-distance billed for the whole 1.3 km of extra driving (the residual 0.46 km being residual matching difference, not refundable).

No fares beyond the meter plus published additions were added (waiting fee $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge), so the disputed $2 the rider noticed is the mileage/time effect of the extra 1.3 km and 11.2 minutes, not an unpublished charge.

The driver has 910 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes, and the rider has 1 upheld route dispute in 90 days; the profile record therefore does not show the driver as a repeat offender and is offered only as background, not as the basis for the finding.

weaknesses: The driver's reroute has real support: F13 shows a genuine accident on the KPE at the MCE tunnel entrance at 18:02 with all lanes closed, and F10 shows KPE at speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) throughout 18:00–18:45 — the other side will argue under RD-4 that the alternative corridor was a reasonable cause, which could exempt the segment entirely.

The rider consented in chat to the ECP route (F7, F8) at 18:10, before the detour began at 18:26; the driver will argue under RD-5 that this is an agreed route change, and my attempt to limit consent to the 'ECP corridor' relies on reading F3's 0.84 km as outside that corridor rather than on an explicit limit in the messages.

The refund I request is small ($1.18) and I do not dispute the other $0.67 of the $1.85 excess-distance charge, so the driver can fairly say F4's billed excess is largely consistent with the driving actually done and the outcome should not be refund_full.

The rider's own profile (F15) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld — including a route dispute — which the driver may use to argue the rider habitually disputes metered fares, though RD-6 lets profiles never decide a case.

Traffic facts only show conditions on KPE/ECP/MCE corridors; there is no record of whether the specific extra 0.84 km stretch on the ECP was itself congested, so a strict RD-4 reading could leave that stretch exempt too.

claims.assertion: The 18:26–18:38 off-route segment (0.84 extra km, F3) was the driver switching from KPE to the ECP after an accident closed the KPE tunnel entrance; the only incident record in the trip window is an accident reported 18:02 sitting 0 m from the optimal route, stating 'All lanes closed. Avoid KPE' (F13). This is corroborating traffic evidence for the replaced stretch of the optimal route, so the segment is exempt under RD-4(a).

Traffic conditions independently confirm the replaced route was impassable: the KPE carried speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) through 18:00–18:45 (F10), while the ECP was free-flowing at band 7 (60–69 km/h) in the same window (F11), matching RD-4(b) corroboration of the incident evidence.

The driver did not change route unilaterally: at 18:10 he told the rider 'KPE is closed at the tunnel entrance because of an accident. I'll go by ECP instead, ok?' (F7) and the rider replied at 18:10 (F8) with 'Ok, thanks for telling me.' The rider's agreement timestamp precedes the start of the off-route segment at 18:26 (F3), so the change satisfies RD-5's 'agreement before the deviation' test and no detour is constituted.

This is a RydeTAXI trip charged on the meter (F6: 16.9 km billed), but any excess-distance component is $1.85 only (F4: 1.3 km × $1.41/km), and under RD-2 an exempted segment generates no refund; the exempt ECP segment therefore carries no refundable amount, so on the route issue alone the action is no_action.

The driver's account shows no route-deviation history to trigger any escalation: 2200 days on platform, rating 4.9, 910 trips in 90 days, 1 dispute with 0 upheld (route: 0) (F16), so the RD-6 repeated-violation condition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met.

The rider's own 90-day record includes 1 upheld route dispute (F15), but profile facts may not decide the finding; they are noted only to show the claim pattern is not attributable to a driver with any upheld route violation (F16).

weaknesses: The GPS record does show a real deviation: an off-route segment 18:26–18:38 adding 0.84 km and reaching up to 2831 m from the optimal route (F3), with actual 16.9 km vs optimal 15.6 km (F1) — the rider will say RD-1 places the burden on the driver to justify every unexplained deviation.

The rider will argue that the driver's route went via the ECP rather than the shorter direct path and that the ride took 32.5 min vs the 21-min estimate (F2) and cost $37.66 (F6), a ~$1.85 excess over the meter for the extra distance (F4).

RD-4(b) alone does not exempt a reroute (MVP guidance), so the driver depends on the RD-4(a) incident link and the RD-5 consent; the rider may argue consent was to 'ECP instead of KPE' only and did not authorise 0.84 km of extra distance or the 2831 m maximum divergence from the optimal path (F3, F8).

points.response: The F13 incident is on KPE at the MCE tunnel entrance at 18:02, but the record and the driver's own chat say he went by the ECP (F7, F11), and the segment the meter charged extra for begins at 18:26 (F3); an event 0 m from one expressway does not exempt the 0.84 km of extra distance actually driven on another corridor, and F13 says 'All lanes closed' — i.e. no traffic could be routed through it, so nothing in F13 addresses whether the ECP line he took was the shortest and most direct available.

F10's KPE band 1 (0–9 km/h) and F11's ECP band 7 (60–69 km/h) at best show which corridor was faster at 18:00–18:45, not that the specific 0.84 km of extra driving recorded 18:26–18:38 was necessary; under RD-4(b) bands are corroboration only and the policy itself states they cannot exempt a segment standing alone, while F12 shows the MCE alternative was itself congested at band 2.

The rider's 18:10 reply agreed to 'go by ECP instead' of KPE (F7, F8) — a corridor choice — and RD-3(b) is explicit that a passenger's agreement to a change does not extend beyond its content, so it does not cover the additional 0.84 km / 2831 m maximum divergence from the optimal path recorded by F3 beginning at 18:26.

The driver's own concession is that the deviation is real and measured (F1: +1.3 km; F3: +0.84 km on one segment), and on a metered RydeTAXI the extra distance is charged at the trip's own rate (F4: 1.3 km × $1.41/km = $1.85 inside the $37.66 total, F6), so the exemption question in RD-4 decides whether 0.84 km of that billed distance is refundable — it is not answered by asserting the exemption.

I agree the driver's record does not meet RD-6's repeated-violation condition (F16: 0 route disputes upheld), which is why I ask for no account flag and only a partial refund; the absence of a prior violation does not excuse this deviation under RD-1.

The rider's profile (F15: 2 disputes in 90 d, 1 upheld) is not a basis for any finding either way, and RD-6 bars profile facts from deciding the case; the deviation is established by F1/F3 and the fare by F4/F6, not by either party's history.

I keep my request but note the computation depends on the extra distance I can attribute to the unexempted stretch: 0.84 km × $1.41/km = $1.18, consistent with F4's $1.85 for the full 1.3 km of extra driving, the remaining ~0.46 km being non-refundable matching residual, so I do not claim the full $1.85.

We accept the trip was metered, but the amount in issue is at larger $1.85 (F4); the rider's own claimed entitlement is $1.18 (C7), not the '$2 over the estimate' pleaded in the complaint. Conceding the mechanism of RD-2 does not concede that any unexempt kilometre exists.

We concede the 18:26–18:38 segment added 0.84 km and reached 2831 m off the optimal line (F3) — our case is not that there was no deviation, but that it is exempt under RD-4(a) and RD-5, and an exempt segment yields no refund under RD-2.

The incident is not a temporal mismatch: F13 was reported at 18:02, sits 0 m from the optimal route, and states 'All lanes closed. Avoid KPE', i.e. it remained live over the optimal route inside the trip window (18:10 pickup, F7), and KPE band 1 (0–9 km/h) is recorded across 18:00–18:45 (F10). That the substitute corridor, ECP, was free-flowing at band 7 (F11) confirms the driver chose the fastest open route as Ryde permits (RD-4(a); RD-1's 'reasonable cause').

We do not rely on the band record alone — RD-4(a) is satisfied by the F13 incident on the optimal route, and F10 only corroborates it as RD-4(b) permits; the rider's own C4 admits F10 corroborates the incident evidence.

The 0.84 km is not a separate 'other corridor': F3 measures the whole off-KPE stretch against the optimal line, and F11 shows the substitute ECP at 60–69 km/h, so the recorded excess is the cost of the one authorised KPE-to-ECP switch, which RD-4(a) exempts.

RD-5's only temporal test is that consent precede the segment, which the rider admits is met here (consent F8 at 18:10, segment start 18:26 per F3); the rider named the ECP corridor and thanked the driver for the notice (F7, F8), so the consented change covers the driving on that corridor.

The $1.18 calculation presupposes an unexempt segment; once F13/F10 exempt the segment under RD-4(a) and F7/F8 consent under RD-5, RD-2 produces a refundable amount of zero and the correct action is no_action, not refund_partial.

We agree no unpublished charge was added — F6 shows waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, surge 1.0× — so FARE-1 gives the rider nothing, and the extra 1.3 km / 11.2 min reflect the closed KPE and light rain (F1, F2, F14, F13).
We agree the profile is background only: F16 shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's flag_account condition is not met and no account action is sought.

notices.text:
We looked into your route dispute and are not issuing a refund.

What decided it: the driver did go off the fastest route for part of the trip, but the motorway tunnel entrance on that route was shut by an accident at the time, and the driver told you beforehand he was taking the other expressway instead — you agreed. Because that stretch was covered by your agreement and a genuine road closure, no part of the fare is refundable.

The amount is $0.00, so no voucher is due.

Nothing changes on your account. Thank you for flagging it.

We looked into the route dispute on this trip and have closed it with no action against you.

What decided it: the GPS did show a short diversion, but the tunnel entrance on the usual route was closed by an accident at the time, and you told the rider before the diversion that you were taking the other expressway, which they agreed to.

No refund is due, so no deduction or voucher applies.

This dispute is not held against you, and no flag has been placed on your account. Thanks for the clear trip record.
